name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Micah Lasher's large fundraising and $10M+ outside support
Open seat after Jerry Nadler's retirement
model.rationale: This Manhattan-based seat carries a +33 Democratic lean, and Lasher has raised $3.3M with over $10M in outside support while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised only about $155K. Markets price the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or unexpected late outside spending for the Republican nominee would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Manhattan district open, but the seat's +33 Democratic partisan lean makes a flip highly unlikely. Micah Lasher enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised $3.3 million and benefited from more than $10.7 million in outside support, against Republican Caroline Shinkle's roughly $155,000 in fundraising.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side at about 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals and the lopsided resource gap, both pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
